messages:
kevin: heads-up — onboarding run for atlas-lite-16b-int4v5 with extended-context=72k revealed a reproducible drift that starts around token 55200. smaller prefill (<=32k) looks identical to float32, but longprefill diverges. attaching quick notes and a tiny repro.

siya: can you share the exact command and the minimal log excerpt?

kevin: command i used:
```bash
./onboard_eval.sh --model=atlas-lite-16b-int4v5 --prefill=56000 --quant=int4v5 --seed=42 --trace=kv,rotary
```
log snippet:
```
[2026-08-01T15:02:10Z] kv.write req=55192 stored=55192
[2026-08-01T15:02:10Z] kv.write req=55205 stored=55205
[2026-08-01T15:02:10Z] kv.write req=55216 stored=16384
[2026-08-01T15:02:10Z] rotary.apply pos=55216 used=16384
[2026-08-01T15:02:10Z] gen token="on" prob_delta=0.018
```

brooke: stored=16384 again but note the pattern: hits happen when global_pos crosses a page-aligned boundary (multiple of 16384). i suspect the int4 LUT precompute uses an allocation sized by PAGE_BITS<<X and we wrap the table index. float path computes cos/sin on the fly so it doesn't exhibit this.

siya: that hypothesis fits with a kernel optimization we merged last quarter: precompute rotary tables into a circular buffer sized at 16k to save memory for small contexts. looks like we didn't gate that by extended-window flag.

kevin: i also saw small diffs in top-k logprobs starting at the first aliased position, but downstream generation amplifies; by token 55280 deltas are >1%.

bench-bot: scheduled differential run: float32 vs int4v5 (seed=42) on goldset-longprefill (N=20 prompts, avg prefill=56k). ETA ~35m. will post per-token perplexity and token-diff histograms.

brooke: immediate mitigations: a) flip the rotary-precompute to dynamic allocation sized to seq_len when seq_len>32k, b) enable kv.safe-evict for canary when prefills exceed 50k to avoid writing into risky ranges. both are low-risk and reversible.

siya: i'll open PR with the dynamic-LUT change and a unit test that exercises seq sizes [16k,32k,49k,72k]. test will assert table_index(req_pos) == table_index_from_scalar(req_pos) for all positions. also adding a CI job variant that runs the longprefill microbench once per day.

kevin: also suggest a micro-bisect: run the same prefill but with quantized kernel toggled off (force float rotary but keep int4 matmul) to see whether positional aliasing alone explains the drift vs combined quant+rope effect. if float-rotary matches float32 then rotary aliasing is root cause.

siya: good call. i'll add that to the bench matrix.

ops: rolling a canary with kv.safe-evict=true and rotary-dyn-lut=false on pool-canary-2 now. will keep traces on for 24h.

bench-bot: differential run complete. summary:
- avg PPL delta (int4v5 vs float32) on longprefill goldset: 0.34 -> 0.78 after token 55200
- token divergence rate jumps from 0.1% to 1.2% post-55200
- float-rotary-int4 path reduced divergence to 0.12% (almost baseline)

brooke: bench outcome strongly suggests rotary table wrap is the dominant cause. proceed with dynamic LUT patch and widen precompute buffer. keep the new unit tests and add a regression entry to the longprefill goldset.

siya: PR opened: #12844 (rotary: dynamic LUT & tests). also added a tiny debug-only tracer that records last 256 kv writes and rotary indices when seq_len>48k. please review.

kevin: nice. after merge let's run a full quant-vs-float diff (same RNG) and a perf check to ensure dynamic LUT doesn't blow latency for common small prompts. if perf cost visible, we can add a switch to use dynamic only when seq>32k.

brooke: agree. i'll own the perf run. tentative rollout plan: merge -> canary 3 nodes -> run full goldset diff -> promote if token-deltas under thresholds.

ops: canary deployed with PR patch on pool-canary-2; traces enabled. will revert kv.safe-evict after we validate.

kevin: thanks all. leaving traces enabled for next 4 runs and saving diffs to /tmp/atlas-longprefill-diffs. ping if you need raw traces. :thumbsup:
